_about: Muzzy's art on the screens (F19). Files are served from public/art/ — made from art/ by `node scripts/art-prep.mjs` (re-run it after changing a file in art/). Button size: s / m / l = picture 3 / 4 / 5.5rem wide. Frame: slice = where its corners end, in the picture's own units (top, right, bottom, left); scale = rem per picture unit (0.0375 ≈ the picture at 60%); ink = the words' colour on the frame's screen. Which art file is what: .planning/research/art-map.md

console._about: The console = the main menu (F21), drawn from Muzzy's mock-up art/Example1.svg. Every number is in that file's own units (its viewBox: 648 wide). size = the whole mock-up; view = the part that shows (the phone-shaped page, from the monitor's bottom edge down to the footer — the GOOPS title and the gear sit under it, written by the game); viewShort = the part shown on a phone on its side (down to the bottom of the laser panel). layers = groups cut out of the mock-up by art-prep, each at its box `at` [x, y, width, height]; strip = bits taken out (they'd show fake numbers or do nothing). periscope.travel = how far it pulls down, as a share of its own height (Example3 has it 362 units lower); grip = the share of it (from the bottom: goggles + bar + arrow) you can grab — its long stem hides behind the monitor. words = where the game writes words over the art: `at` + `text` (letter size in mock-up units).
console._monitorDrop: F35 (Muzzy 2026-10-24: 'the console monitor can come down much lower. like 2x the distance, so long as the top of the graphic isn't in view. this will give more room for the company message'): how far (mock-up units) the monitor and its screen hang lower than the mock-up at rest. 78 = twice what showed before. A lesson step that outlines the periscope lifts it back to 0, so the periscope shows.

words._bottomRow: F70 (Muzzy 2026-10-24): the bottom row reads version · RANK SELECT · MuzzyMade © 2026. rankSelect = the Dev Kit's rank tool (a button; its box is centred on the row and taller, so the button's 44 px tap target sits on the row).

crt._about: F32 (Muzzy, 2026-10-19): the monitor's screen IS the lesson message at the console. Its words sit in words.hint (smaller and higher than the mock-up, so they stay on the screen, off the bezel); a lesson line that needs more room makes the screen slide down past its bezel like a toaster. screen / bezel = the monitor art's colours (cls-51 / cls-56 in Example1.svg); bezelWidth = the bezel's thickness at the sides and bottom; screenLeft / screenTop / screenWidth / screenBottom = the screen's edges (mock-up units: the game draws the screen over the art's, so a longer line can slide it down seamlessly); radius = its corners.

repairs._about: F24: the repair panels' moving parts, drawn by the game over the panels (art-prep strips the same parts out of them: stripClasses = the knobs, the dial face and the lamps; strip = the three arcade buttons). Boxes are [x, y, width, height] in the mock-up's units, read off Example1.svg. viewShort = what a phone on its side shows mid-shift: just the three panels (the way back is then the Back to the tank button). knob = the slider knob's share of its track (50.23 / 175.86). Laser: sliders in the order row 1 left, row 1 right, row 2 left, row 2 right, each with its two lamps [left end, right end]. Controls: the dial, its four corner lamps (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left) and the angle (degrees clockwise from up) the dial's arrow points at each. Visor (RESET LIGHTS): the up/down slider, its top lamp and its bottom lamp, and the three buttons top to bottom with their lamps. F32 (Muzzy: the slider sat too low and the bottom lamp overlapped it): the track is cut out of the panel into its own file (track: its shapes by colour class, from = where the mock-up had it) and drawn at `slider` — 92% of its size and higher, so both lamps fit above and below it.
